headline: 4 contracts catalogued across Ethereum and BSC from explorer name-tag search; 14+ chains unverified; no official deployments doc found.

findings.text: Etherscan name-tag search surfaced 2 Ethereum contracts: 0xE2fE530C047f2d85298b07D9333C05737f1435fB (TrustSwap: Team Finance Lock, AdminUpgradeabilityProxy) and 0x64D06dcc12fA07e302f052a9F5BC1aa11e29D9E2 (TrustSwap: Team Finance Vesting/VestingFactory). BscScan search surfaced 0x0C89C0407775dd89b12918B9c0aa42Bf96518820 (TrustSwap: Team Finance Security on BSC, EIP-1967 Transparent Proxy). Parent ecosystem SWAP token at 0xCC4304A31d09258b0029eA7FE63d032f52e44EFe on Ethereum confirmed via trustswap.com.
handbook.team.finance (docs) was fetched; it describes services but contains no canonical deployed-contracts address page. No deployed_contracts_doc URL could be pinned.

The pinned audit_link (https://www.team.finance/file/audit.pdf) resolved to a GitBook security page, not a raw PDF. A Chainsulting audit PDF for Team Finance was found at https://github.com/chainsulting/Smart-Contract-Security-Audits/blob/master/Team%20Finance/02_Smart%20Contract%20Audit%20Team%20Finance.pdf (GitHub blob, PDF not parseable). Website lists Hacken, Certik, and BailSec as auditors. No in-scope contract addresses could be extracted from audit PDFs this run.

GitHub org 'team-finance' confirmed to exist (team-finance/team-finance-interface repository surfaced). No deployment artifact files (broadcast JSON, hardhat-deploy JSON, addresses.json, etc.) were successfully fetched this run due to tool-call limits. Raw GitHub org repo listing was not accessible (allowlist rejection for github.com/team-finance org page).

BSC chain: 0x0C89C0407775dd89b12918B9c0aa42Bf96518820 surfaced from BscScan. BscScan multichain info notes the same implementation is cross-referenced to Etherscan, BaseScan, and Polygonscan. Base, Polygon, Avalanche, Pulse, Arbitrum, Blast, Cronos, Fantom, Kava, Flare, Klaytn, Odyssey, Mantle, LUKSO, and Berachain were not directly searched due to tool-call exhaustion.

VestingFactory at 0x64D06dcc12fA07e302f052a9F5BC1aa11e29D9E2 is a factory contract. Children were not enumerated due to tool-call limits. Lock contract 0xE2fE530C047f2d85298b07D9333C05737f1435fB is an AdminUpgradeabilityProxy that holds locked tokens directly (not a factory pattern), with multiple historical upgrades to implementation contracts.

Role taxonomy applied: Lock contract = vault (proxy); Vesting = factory; BSC contract = vault (proxy). SWAP token = token (parent ecosystem). Implementation contracts for the proxy (0x6Dd27F2b...8280359f1 on Ethereum) discovered from upgrade history but full addresses truncated in search snippet — recorded as unknowns.
All 4 addresses in admin_addresses[] trace to search result snippets from etherscan.io, bscscan.com, and trustswap.com. No addresses added from memory or inference alone.

rationale.verdict: Discovery run walked the official website, docs, security page, Etherscan/BscScan name-tag search, GitHub org search, and Chainsulting audit blob. 4 contracts catalogued: 2 on Ethereum (Lock proxy + Vesting factory), 1 on BSC (Security/Lock proxy), and 1 parent SWAP token on Ethereum. 15 additional chains from protocol.chains remain unverified due to tool-call exhaustion. No canonical deployed-contracts doc was found.

protocol_metadata.about: Team Finance is a non-custodial token management platform built by TrustSwap Inc. that allows blockchain projects to lock team tokens and liquidity-pool tokens in time-released smart contract vaults. Users can also create vesting schedules, staking reward pools, airdrops, payroll streams, and batch token sends via a single application. The protocol operates across 30+ blockchains and holds approximately $500M in total value locked as of mid-2026. Core lock and vesting contracts are upgradeable proxies (AdminUpgradeabilityProxy / EIP-1967) audited by Hacken, Certik, BailSec, and Chainsulting.
